# 1.2.115 - Doors and Keep Watch: Shut the Door, Force the Door, Pick the Lock and Keep Watch as rows of the Infiltrate tile, each rolled on the GMs' record; Repair the Lock as a project; a Reroll that replays the new rolls

Stage E74, built on 1.2.114 (E69) on the same work line. Its commits are C1+C2 f7d9fb2, C3 75aeb8d, C4 4f21e9e, C6
f64d5f6, d8905af, C5's Broken column 573ddad, the fix 32b4c1a, the glyphs a123ff1, C7 68ec08d, C5 e337ac9 and
55dab3e, with the STATUS commits 97ef581, 80a8140, 3e8ea61 and 40a920f (no code). C7 also replays E93's and E69's
rolls; those parts are named in 1.2.113's and 1.2.114's notes. In plain words:

- **Shut the Door.** A Body roll, drawn on the primary GM's browser. In a room with at most two doors that open, not
  another's bedroom, not with a body the player knows of and nobody found, the GM keeps a barricade whose strength is
  the roll's total. A walk in through a door is refused on the walker's own browser and by the GMs' audit ("The door
  does not give."); a passage, a breach or a tunnel goes through, and a GM moving a token is never stopped. It comes
  down when its author leaves the room, at the time of day's end, at an Eclipse's start and at the season reset.
  Someone stopped at the door sends the barricade's author's owners a card, "Someone tries to get in", with no name,
  one card a barricade a quarter of a minute.
- **Force the Door.** A Body roll against everything that holds a door next to the character's room, all at once: a
  barricade by its strength (a tie holds), a GM's or a bedroom's lock and a seal at 18, a critical all. A forced lock
  stays broken until repaired; a forced seal is lifted for its time of day. The rooms next to either room hear a banging
  from it, with no name; the two rooms learn who it was; a bedroom's owner gets a card - on a pass, and on a miss with
  Despair.
- **Pick the Lock.** A Shadow roll against 16 for cover, then a Hand roll against 15 (18 clean), both drawn on the GM.
  At a door held by a lock or a seal (never a barricade) an open walks the picker in - the GM's move - and the lock stays
  locked. The room beyond sees who it was below the cover; a bedroom's owner is warned of an open below 18 and of a miss
  with Despair.
- **Keep Watch.** A Body roll against 12, declared before an Eclipse (struck through in one and before the Night
  Eclipse). At the Eclipse's start the post is the watcher's room: a card of who is in it, a card for each settled
  crossing into or out of it (never which way), a summary at its end. The watcher is held to the post: a walk out of it
  in the Eclipse is put back by the primary GM. A miss with Despair marks a Sanity.
- **Repair the Lock.** A project preset (Hand, Trivial), offered in Start New where a door of the builder's room has a
  broken lock, one project a door; its completion mends the lock. In Room Setup's Doors tab a **Broken** column shows a
  lock a Force or a breach broke; unticked and applied, the lock is mended.
- **Remnants.** A barricade leaves a subtle trace, a forced door an evident one where it was heard, a pick one by its
  roll (a miss with Despair evident, a miss with Hope and 15-17 subtle, 18 and over hidden).
- **A Reroll of these rolls** is replayed on the primary GM (until now a Reroll of any of them told the GMs "this roll
  left no lasting effect" and left the first result standing): a barricade's strength, a watch kept or let go, and a
  door forced or a lock picked by a higher roll. A door forced, a lock picked (the picker walked in) and a room action's
  effects stand when the new roll is lower, and the GMs' line says so.
- **The Infiltrate window** has its seven rows. Shut and Force wear different glyphs in both themes (Monokuma Legacy:
  Font Awesome's road barrier and fist; Stained Glass: E48's own drawings for the six rows).

Nothing in this version ran at a real table or on a Foundry server; what was measured was measured headless. Below,
an R number names one of the module's own tests (`game.drpg.runTests()`), and a scenario one of the headless
harness's multi-browser runs.

## Before installing

- **No world migration.** No clause was added to `migrate.mjs`, and no language key of the module's was removed or
  renamed.
- **New stored data**: two GM stores, `barricades` (strength, author) and `watches`, kept in the GMs' browsers; one
  public region flag, `ROOM_FLAGS.barricaded` (`true` and nothing else), on a barricaded room. That flag is held by
  every browser: a console reads which rooms are barricaded, never by whom or how strongly (the owner's DA47; Known
  gaps).
- **New bridge roads**: `door.shut`, `door.force`, `door.pick`, `watch.declare` and `door.knock`, each judged on the
  primary GM. Two new refusal reasons, `barricaded` and `onWatch`, said to the player in their language. With no GM
  connected, none of the four actions can be taken, and nothing is paid.

## The owner's answers

- The decisions the plan names (as it records them, translated, docs/dev/plans/E74.md): DA9 - Force breaks a lock
  until it is repaired, Pick opens for the picker only; DA25 - Shut the Door only in a room with at most two exits, the
  own bedroom yes, another's no, not with an unfound body the player knows of; DA28, DA48 - seven rows in one list,
  Repair the Lock a preset at Trivial; DA29 - Pick and Force on bedrooms, every GM lock and the seal, never Chained or
  the courtroom in a trial; DA30 - the owner learns on a careless open and on a miss with Despair, every attempt leaves
  a Remnant by its band; DA31, DA52 - Pick 15 (18 clean), Force on a lock 18, the same at a seal; DA34 - Keep Watch
  declared before the Eclipse, live cards with names, a summary at the end; DA43 - the rooms next door hear a banging,
  no name; DA44 - one hindrance die on the opening roll at a watch of 18 and over (not built: Known gaps); DA47 - a
  public "barricaded" flag with no author or strength, with a known-leaks row and a README paragraph; 01.11 (D197) -
  the Night Eclipse keeps free placement, Keep Watch struck through in Night.
- **12.11.2026**, on the shots of E93, E69 and E74, as the coordinator relayed it: "na razie wygladaja dobrze". No
  changes asked.
- Defaults taken, each "default, owner may revise" (the coordinator, 12.11.2026; docs/dev/e74/STATUS.md): "open exits"
  are the neighbours a GM's lock does not shut; a barricade's strength is the total whatever it is, a critical adds
  nothing; not in an Eclipse, not by a character the GMs hold dead, one barricade a room; the Mastermind is stopped by
  a barricade like anyone; Keep Watch keeps a watch at 12 or more, a miss keeps none; a barricade gives only to a roll
  above its strength; forcing is allowed in an Eclipse; a Chained character may not force; the player's card says
  "Nothing holds the door" when nothing did; Repair the Lock as a preset row (Q-E74-1); the Locked column kept beside
  Broken (Q-E74-4).

## Known gaps

- **DA44 is not built**, the hindrance die at a watch of 18 and over. A drawn roll's dice are the GM's own list, and a
  die the GM adds that the roller's window did not is named on a card to the roller. The killer's browser cannot know
  the victim watches (the watch is the GMs'), so the die would be named to the killer, telling them of the watch. A
  question for the owner: say "a hindrance die" in the killer's window without saying why, or roll it on the GM
  unnamed.
- **DA9's pass is not built as planned**: an open is used at once (the GM walks the picker in); there is no pass that
  lasts until the picker leaves the room. Default, owner may revise.
- **DA30's warning** to a bedroom's owner is sent at once, wherever the owner is, not at their next entry.
- **The barricade's public flag** (DA47) is the module's on purpose; its known-leaks row and README paragraph are
  not in this line's commits (proposed in docs/dev/e74/STATUS.md, "For the coordinator").
- **Not taken back by a lower Reroll**: a door forced, a lock picked (the picker walked in), a room action's effects,
  and a Dash's crossings already spent. Each line says so.
- **Force the Door has no legal control in scenario 33** (Aiko's room in the harness has no neighbour); tier 2's E74-T2
  is its legal road, judged as the primary judges a player's packet.
- **E53's ledger counters** (Q-E74-5) are not in this release.
- **The look** was seen in Chromium on the harness's pages (audit/style-harness.html), both themes, EN and PL, at
  1366x768, in two rounds: the Infiltrate window with its seven rows, Force's and Pick's windows, Room Setup's Doors
  tab, and Start New offering Repair the Lock. Not Foundry, no Font Awesome (Monokuma Legacy's rows show no icon
  there), no window frame; the cards are not drawn there. Seen in Monokuma Legacy PL: the Doors tab's headers
  "Zamknięte" and "Bez prywatności" are cut in their narrow columns - already so at f22a7e87, before the Broken column;
  not this stage's, left as it is.
- **Scenario 61's D5**: measured, not this line's code (1.2.113's Known gaps).
